text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Foreign ownership ceilings scrapped in transport, banking, insurance, communications and farming sectors.
- Secretary General of Islamic Action Front has resigned over disagreements about participation in parliamentary elections.

- Government planning to issue laws on intellectual property, competition and prevention of monopolies, protection of national output, free trade zones and investment funds, rapporteur of senate economic committee says.
- Foreigners allowed to take 100 percent ownership in five sectors.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali heading for Bahrain today.
- Amman court sentences murderer to death.
- Economists and investors welcome decision to cancel restrictions on foreign currency transfer.
- Higher investment council lifts ceiling on foreign investment in Jordanian financial markets in banking, insurance, communications and agriculture sectors.
- Government expected to pass six temporary laws on the economy soon.
- Lloyds Register says it conducting inspections in Aqaba under U.N. instructions and would stop if told to do so by U.N.
